title: Cases eligible for a small claim
passage: The claim limit is S$20,000, or S$30,000 with a Memorandum of Consent from both parties. Claims must be filed within two years of the event creating the cause of action. Goods and services contracts are among the eligible categories. Claims must be served on a respondent in Singapore. The CJTS pre-filing assessment is not conclusive. Bankruptcy or insolvency may require permission.

title: How to file and serve a small claim
passage: File through CJTS using the pre-filing assessment ID, parties' details, claim summary and supporting PDFs. For a business respondent, prepare an ACRA profile obtained within one month of filing. A Memorandum of Consent is required for claims above S$20,000 up to S$30,000. Filing, service of the claim and filing the Declaration of Service are separate steps.

title: File a small claim
passage: The process covers eligibility, filing and service, online dispute resolution, consultation, and a possible hearing. Parties may choose eNegotiation or eMediation to resolve the dispute online.

title: Guide to SCT AI-generated summaries
passage: CJTS offers AI-generated summaries of the claimant's or respondent's case through the AI Summaries tab in an active case.

title: GenAI guide for court users
passage: Court users are responsible for their court documents. Verify AI-assisted content and references against reliable sources. Do not fabricate or tamper with evidence. Be prepared to identify AI-assisted portions and explain their verification. Asking another AI is not sufficient verification. Protect confidential information.

title: Legal help and support
passage: The Singapore Courts provide a Legal Help Finder and information on seeking help for civil and tribunal matters. Assistance depends on the relevant scheme and circumstances.
